docs.title: Barrier
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Barrier<I, O> : Operation<I, O>

An Operation that needs its whole input before any output, so it is not split: sort, take and reduce are barriers.

docs.title: Bool
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Bool : Scalar

The truth values true and false: a Scalar with equality and no order.

docs.title: Bytes
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Bytes : {Scalar, Orderable}

A finite sequence of octets, ordered octet by octet as unsigned numbers, a shorter prefix first (HQL-0053 part 1). No literal produces one: Bytes("hello") is the UTF-8 encoding of a text, and encoding converts hex and base64 text. It prints as 0x and lowercase hex, and a text format writes it as base64.

fn Bytes(text: String) : Bytes

The UTF-8 encoding of text: Bytes("hé") holds three octets.

docs.title: Collection
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Collection<T> : Iterable<T>

A finite multiset of occurrences, unordered, with no runtime representation. size(c) is the number of occurrences, count(c, x) the number equal to x, and contains(c, x) holds where count(c, x) > 0; so size(c) is the sum of count(c, x) over the distinct values in c.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Data = union { Scalar, Seq<Data>, Map<String, Data> }

An open tree whose keys belong to whoever wrote them: what a YAML or JSON document is. It is a union of exactly three alternatives: a Scalar leaf, a sequence of trees, or a String-keyed map of trees.

fn Data<F : Format>(text: String, as: Type<F>) : Data

text parsed in the format as: Data("[1, 2]", Json) is [1, 2], and s | Data(Yaml) is one call. The format is one whose decoder reads Data: Json, JsonLines, Yaml or Csv. A framed format, JsonLines or Csv, gives the list of its records; Json or Yaml gives one document. Text that does not parse fails at run time.

docs.title: DataContract
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type DataContract : Data

The supertype of an open contract: a structural type declared type D : DataContract = {…} is a view over Data with at least its declared fields, and is validated as a contract. It is open by being Data; no Data is written beside it.

docs.title: Date
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Date : {Scalar, Orderable}

A proleptic Gregorian calendar date, ordered by time: Date("2026-10-24"). It is written as its ISO 8601 text.

fn Date(text: String) : Date

The Date an ISO 8601 date reads as: Date("2026-10-24"). Any other text, a time part included, is an evaluation error naming it; to_date gives none instead.

fn Date(*, year: Int, month: Int, day: Int) : Date

The Date of a year, a month 1..12 and a day of that month: Date(year = 2026, month = 10, day = 24). A part out of range, February 30 among them, is an evaluation error.

docs.title: DateTime
docs.text:
In std/core.

type DateTime : {Scalar, Orderable}

A date and a time of day with no zone or offset, ordered by time: DateTime("2026-10-24T09:30:00"). It names a wall-clock reading and becomes an Instant only through a zone.

fn DateTime(text: String) : DateTime

The DateTime an ISO 8601 date and time with no offset reads as: DateTime("2026-10-24T09:30:00"), with up to nine fraction digits. Text with an offset or a Z is an Instant's, and an evaluation error here.

fn DateTime(date: Date, *, hour: Int = 0, minute: Int = 0, second: Int = 0, nanosecond: Int = 0) : DateTime

The DateTime of date at a time of day: DateTime(Date("2026-10-24"), hour = 9, minute = 30). A part out of range, hour = 24 among them, is an evaluation error.

docs.title: Decimal
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Decimal : {Scalar, Orderable}

An exact decimal number, written with a decimal point and no suffix (2.50), ordered by value: 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 is true. See Decimal.

docs.title: Diagnostic
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Diagnostic : DataContract { phase : String kind : String severity : String disposition : String message : String origin? : String span : Data labels? : List<Data> help? : List<String> expected? : String found? : Data element? : Data bindings? : Data trace? : List<Data> source? : Data violations? : List<Violation> }

A diagnostic a run delivered, read back as data: its phase, kind, severity and disposition, its message, and where it points, origin and span, a {start, end} byte range. The fields a producer fills where they apply are optional: labels, help, expected, found, element, bindings, trace, source and the violations of a contract read. source(file(p), JsonLines) | Diagnostic reads what --diagnostics-format json wrote.

trait Div

Division: a / b over a type implementing Div is a.div(b).

docs.title: Duration
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Duration : {Scalar, Orderable}

A signed length of time in nanoseconds, ordered by length: Duration("PT1H30M"). + and - add and subtract two; a day is 24 hours, and a month or a year is no Duration.

fn Duration(text: String) : Duration

The Duration ISO 8601 duration text reads as, in weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds: Duration("PT1H30M"), Duration("P2DT3H"). The year and month designators are an evaluation error, since their length depends on the date they start from.

fn Duration(*, days: Int = 0, hours: Int = 0, minutes: Int = 0, seconds: Int = 0, millis: Int = 0, nanos: Int = 0) : Duration

The Duration of the sum of its parts, each signed: Duration(hours = 1, minutes = 30) is PT1H30M.

docs.title: Elementwise
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Elementwise<I, O> : Operation<I, O>

An Operation whose result for each element depends on that element alone, so it may run over any split of its input: map and filter are elementwise. Piped a collection of I, it runs over each element, and its body reads its one element and nothing else: long : Elementwise<Int, Bool> = n => n > 300.

docs.text:
In std/core.

trait Eq

Equality: a == b and a != b over a type implementing Eq call its eq.

docs.title: Float
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Float : {Scalar, Orderable}

A 64-bit binary floating-point number, written with the suffix f (2.5f), ordered by value.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Format

The category of formats: how bytes are documents. Parsing text into Data, and every reading and writing operation of io, takes a Format; the formats and their codecs are the format module's.

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
In std/core.

trait Index<T>

A position: xs[i] over a type implementing Index is xs.at(i), the element there or its absence. T is the element type, which each implementation names: E : Index<T> leaves T to the type E is.

docs.title: Members
docs.text: fn at(self, position: Int) : Option<T>

docs.title: Instant
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Instant : {Scalar, Orderable}

A point on the UTC timeline with nanosecond precision, ordered by time: Instant("2026-10-24T07:30:00Z"). It is written in RFC 3339, in UTC.

fn Instant(text: String) : Instant

The Instant RFC 3339 text reads as, with Z or an offset: Instant("2026-10-24T09:30:00+02:00") is 2026-10-24T07:30:00Z. Text without an offset is a DateTime's, and an evaluation error here.

fn Instant(*, unix_seconds: Int) : Instant

The Instant unix_seconds whole seconds after 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, before it when negative.

fn Instant(*, unix_millis: Int) : Instant

The Instant unix_millis milliseconds after 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.

docs.title: Int
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Int : {Scalar, Orderable}

A 64-bit whole number, ordered by value: 7 / 2 is 3, and 7 % 2 is 1.

docs.title: Invalid
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Invalid : DataContract { contract : String value : Data violations : List<Violation> }

A value that did not read as a contract, and every reason why: its contract, the value, and the violations.

docs.title: Is
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Is<T>

What a predicate that tests its parameter's type, x => x | is(U), gives: a Bool that, where true, holds the parameter at U. A parameter of type T -> Is<U> takes only such a predicate, and binds U to the type it tests.

docs.title: Iterable
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Iterable<T>

A value whose elements can each be visited: the bound an operation states when it only visits each value. Finiteness, order and uniqueness are not part of it.

docs.title: List
docs.text:
In std/core.

type List<T> : Seq<T>

A sequence of materialized occurrences; repeated traversal preserves positions. A list literal [1, 2, 3] is a List<Int>.

fn List<T>(xs: Seq<T>) : List<T>

The List of the elements of xs, in order: List([1, 2]) is [1, 2].

docs.title: Map
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Map<K, V>

Materialized associations from distinct keys of K to values of V; not a Collection. Its keys are a Set<K>, and a lookup gives an Option<V>.

fn Map<K, V>(keys: Seq<K>, values: Seq<V>) : Map<K, V>

The Map from each of keys to the value at the same position in values. The two are equally long, and a repeated key fails at run time.

docs.title: Mul
docs.text:
In std/core.

trait Mul

Multiplication: a * b over a type implementing Mul is a.mul(b).

docs.title: Members
docs.text: fn mul(self, other: Self) : Self

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Operation<I, O>

A function from I to O that also carries its shape: what an executor may assume about splitting the step. A value of one is called as an I -> O function is, and a lambda bound at one is an operation on equal terms with map or filter.

docs.title: Option
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Option<T>

An optional value of T: present, holding one T, or absent. Absence is an ordinary sum type; there is no null. The ways out are the option module's, and each says what absence means.

docs.title: Ord
docs.text:
In std/core.

trait Ord

Order: a < b and the other comparisons over a type implementing Ord call its compare. A type implementing Ord is Orderable: sort, min and max take it, and its compare gives the order.

docs.title: Members
docs.text: fn compare(self, other: Self) : Ordering

docs.title: Orderable
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Orderable

A type whose values have a total order: of any two values of the type, one comes first or the two are equal. compare, <, sort, min and max take it, and SortedMap keys are of it. Order is a property of the element, not of a collection holding it.

docs.title: OrderedMap
docs.text:
In std/core.

type OrderedMap<K, V> : Map<K, V>

A Map whose keys keep their construction positions: its keys are a Seq<K>. K need not be Orderable. Viewed as a Map, its keys are a set.

fn OrderedMap<K, V>(keys: Seq<K>, values: Seq<V>) : OrderedMap<K, V>

The OrderedMap from each of keys to the value at the same position in values, its keys in the order of keys.

docs.title: Ordering
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Ordering

The result of compare(a, b): Less, Equal or Greater. compare(1, 2) is Less.

docs.title: Pair
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Pair<A, B> { first : A second : B }

Two values held together, each at its own type: what zip, enumerate, entries and join produce, and what Pair(first = a, second = b) builds.

docs.title: Partition
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Partition<I, O> : Operation<I, O>

An Operation that regroups its input by a key, each group running independently and completing in any order: group is one.

docs.title: Range
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Range { start? : Int end? : Int }

A window of positions, what a slice takes: xs[a:b] is xs[Range(start = a, end = b)], and a bound left out is absent. A negative bound counts from the end: "hello"[-2:] is "lo".

docs.title: Reduction
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Reduction<I, O> : Operation<I, O>

An Operation that collapses its whole input to one value through a combiner the runtime holds, so each split may be reduced and the results combined: size combines by addition, contains by disjunction.

docs.title: Rem
docs.text:
In std/core.

trait Rem

Remainder: a % b over a type implementing Rem is a.rem(b).

docs.title: Members
docs.text: fn rem(self, other: Self) : Self

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Result<T, E>

A computation that may have failed: ok(value) with a T, or err(error) with an E. The ways out are the result module's, and mirror Option's; there is no unwrap.

docs.title: Scalar
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Scalar

A leaf: a value with no parts of its own. Being a leaf and having an order are separate contracts: Bool is a Scalar and not Orderable.

docs.title: Seq
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Seq<T> : {Collection<T>, Stream<T>}

A finite stream: a collection in which every occurrence has exactly one position in 0 .. size(c) - 1. Positional order does not require T : Orderable.

docs.title: Set
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Set<T> : Collection<T>

Materialized distinct values under HQL equality: count(s, x) <= 1. Traversal order is not a semantic guarantee.

fn Set<T>(xs: Collection<T>) : Set<T>

The Set of the distinct elements of xs.

docs.title: Slice
docs.text:
In std/core.

trait Slice

A part: xs[a:b] over a type implementing Slice is xs.slice(Range(start = a, end = b)), a value of the type itself.

docs.title: Members
docs.text: fn slice(self, range: Range) : Self

docs.title: SortedMap
docs.text:
In std/core.

type SortedMap<K, V> : OrderedMap<K, V> where K : Orderable

An OrderedMap whose key positions follow the intrinsic total order of K.

fn SortedMap<K : Orderable, V>(keys: Seq<K>, values: Seq<V>) : SortedMap<K, V>

The SortedMap from each of keys to the value at the same position in values, its keys in the order of K.

docs.title: Stream
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type Stream<T> : Iterable<T>

An ordered, possibly unending run of values x0, x1, x2, .... Size, membership and global order are undefined on a stream: each requires a last value.

docs.title: String
docs.text:
In std/core.

type String : {Scalar, Orderable}

Text, ordered character by character: "ab" + "cd" is "abcd", and "hello"[1] is "e".

docs.title: Sub
docs.text:
In std/core.

trait Sub

Subtraction: a - b over a type implementing Sub is a.sub(b).

docs.title: Members
docs.text: fn sub(self, other: Self) : Self

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Type<T>

A type written as an argument: is(Card), of_type(Card). A parameter of type Type<U> takes a type name and binds U to the type it names.

docs.title: TypeContract
docs.text:
In std/core.

abstract type TypeContract

The supertype of a closed contract: a structural type declared type C : TypeContract = {…} has exactly its declared fields, and is validated as a contract.

docs.title: Validator
docs.text:
In std/core.

trait Validator

A check a value passes: a trait extending Validator is a validator trait. validate f with V holds where V's validate of f is true, and a field declared f: V reads as the type implementing V, held to it.

docs.title: Members
docs.text: fn validate(self) : Bool

docs.title: Violation
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Violation : DataContract { contract : String path : List<String> kind : String rule : String text : String expected? : String actual? : Data severity : String = "error" message : String }

One reason a value does not read as a contract, as validate(T) reports it. kind is "missing", "undeclared", "type" or "rule"; rule is the rule's identity, Contract.name, or Contract.n for the n-th unnamed rule; path leads from the value to the field, [] for the value itself.

docs.title: Window
docs.text:
In std/core.

type Window<T>

One row's place in its ordered partition under over: the rows with its key, in the order over gives them, and its position among them. It has no fields: the seq module's window functions read it, and a window does not leave the into it is handed to. See Windows.

docs.title: std/crypto
docs.text:
module crypto

Keys, signatures, MACs, password hashes and encryption. An algorithm and a key format are each named by a type, as a format is: PublicKey(text, Pem, Ed25519). A key's type carries its algorithm, so a key of one algorithm used where another is named is a check error. PrivateKey, KeyPair and SecretKey are Secret: no format writes one, == does not compare them, and each prints redacted.

  • KeyAlgorithm — An asymmetric key algorithm.
  • Signing — An asymmetric key algorithm.
  • Agreement — An asymmetric key algorithm.
  • Ed25519 — An asymmetric key algorithm.
  • P256 — An asymmetric key algorithm.
  • Rsa — An asymmetric key algorithm.
  • X25519 — An asymmetric key algorithm.
  • SecretAlgorithm — A symmetric algorithm: a Cipher encrypts, a Mac authenticates.
  • Cipher — A symmetric algorithm: a Cipher encrypts, a Mac authenticates.
  • Mac — A symmetric algorithm: a Cipher encrypts, a Mac authenticates.
  • Aes256Gcm — A symmetric algorithm: a Cipher encrypts, a Mac authenticates.
  • ChaCha20Poly1305 — A symmetric algorithm: a Cipher encrypts, a Mac authenticates.
  • HmacSha256 — A symmetric algorithm: a Cipher encrypts, a Mac authenticates.
  • HmacSha512 — A symmetric algorithm: a Cipher encrypts, a Mac authenticates.
  • Secret — The values that hold private key material: no format encodes one, == does not compare them, and each prints redacted.
  • PublicKey — A public key of algorithm A.
  • PrivateKey — A private key of algorithm A.
  • KeyPair — A private key and its public key.
  • SecretKey — A symmetric key of algorithm A.
  • KeyFormat — How one key is text.
  • Pem — How one key is text.
  • Jwk — How one key is text.
  • OpenSsh — How one key is text.
  • Age — How one key is text.
  • to_public_key — The public key self holds in format, or none.
  • to_private_key — The private key self holds in format, or none.
  • read_public_key — The public key a file holds in format.
  • read_private_key — The private key a file holds in format.
  • to_text — self written in format: key.to_text(OpenSsh) is an ssh-ed25519 AAAA… line.
  • to_der — self as SPKI DER.
  • export_private — The private key material of self written in format, encrypted under passphrase where one is given: PKCS #8 with scrypt and AES-256-CBC for Pem, bcrypt-pbkdf and AES-256-CTR for OpenSsh.
  • public — The public key of a private key.
  • thumbprint — The RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint of self: base64url, unpadded, of the SHA-256 of its canonical JWK.
  • generate_key_pair — A new key pair from the host's cryptographically secure generator.
  • generate_secret_key — A new symmetric key from the host generator: 32 octets for a cipher and HmacSha256, 64 for HmacSha512.
  • sign — The signature of the octets of self by key.
  • sign_data — The signature of canonical(self), the RFC 8785 text of the tree, so two trees equal under HQL equality have one signature.
  • verify — Whether signature is key's signature of self: false, never an error, for a signature of another key, of the wrong length or malformed.
  • verify_data — Whether signature is key's signature of canonical(self).
  • p256_signature_from_der — The r || s form of an ASN.1 DER ECDSA P-256 signature, as OpenSSL writes one, or none where self is not one.
  • mac — The HMAC tag of self under key: 32 octets for HmacSha256, 64 for HmacSha512.
  • verify_mac — Whether tag is the MAC tag of self under key, compared in time independent of where it first differs.
  • hash_password — The Argon2id hash of self under a new 16-octet salt from the host generator, as a PHC string: $argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$…$….
  • verify_password — Whether self is the password hash was made from, under the hash's own parameters.
  • encrypt — The authenticated encryption of self under key, with aad bound to it and not encrypted: a new 12-octet nonce from the host generator, then the ciphertext, then the 16-octet tag.
  • decrypt — The plaintext of self under key and aad, or none where self is not an encryption of anything under them: shorter than 28 octets, a changed octet anywhere, a wrong key or a wrong aad.
  • encrypt_to — The age encryption of self to every key of recipients: any one of their private keys decrypts it.
  • decrypt_with — The plaintext of the age message self for identity, or none where it is not a message to that key or has been changed.
  • encrypt_with_passphrase — The age encryption of self under a passphrase, by age's scrypt recipient with work factor 18.
  • decrypt_with_passphrase — The plaintext of the age message self under passphrase, or none.
  • armor — The ASCII armor of an age message: -----BEGIN AGE ENCRYPTED FILE-----.
  • unarmor — The age message an armored text holds, or none.
  • EncryptedEnd — An endpoint whose writes are age-encrypted to recipients and stored in endpoint.
  • DecryptedEnd — An endpoint whose contents are those of a replayable endpoint, age-decrypted.
  • DecryptedLive — An endpoint whose contents are those of a live endpoint, age-decrypted.
  • encrypted_to — endpoint, its writes age-encrypted to recipients.
  • decrypted_with — endpoint, its contents age-decrypted with identity.

docs.title: encrypt
docs.text:
In std/crypto.

effectful fn encrypt<C : Cipher>(self: Bytes, key: SecretKey<C>, *, aad: Bytes = Bytes("")) : Bytes

The authenticated encryption of self under key, with aad bound to it and not encrypted: a new 12-octet nonce from the host generator, then the ciphertext, then the 16-octet tag. Under random nonces a key takes at most 2^32 encryptions, for either cipher.

The authenticated encryption of the UTF-8 octets of self.

docs.title: export_private
docs.text:
In std/crypto.

fn export_private<F : KeyFormat, A : KeyAlgorithm>(self: PrivateKey<A>, format: Type<F>, *, passphrase: String = "") : String

The private key material of self written in format, encrypted under passphrase where one is given: PKCS #8 with scrypt and AES-256-CBC for Pem, bcrypt-pbkdf and AES-256-CTR for OpenSsh. The result is a String, and no longer redacted.

docs.title: std/format
docs.text:
module format

The formats, how bytes are read as values and how values are written as text, and the codec contracts over them.

A format is a type narrowing Format, the category core declares. It names an external representation and, where it applies, its framing: Lines is text framed one record per line, JsonLines one JSON document per line. A format is not the text it encodes, so none narrows String, and it is not Format<T>, since one format encodes many value structures. Whether what is read ends is a property of the source, not of the format: source(file(p), Lines) is a Seq<String> and source(stdin, Lines) a Stream<String>.

A String is always UTF-8. Every format that holds text reads and writes UTF-8, and decoding bytes that are not UTF-8 is a decoding error.

  • Text — The plain-text format: read, the whole input is one String; written, a value is its display text, and a String its characters as they are.
  • Lines — The format of text framed one record per line: read, each line is one String; written, each element of a collection is one line: [1, 2] | lines is "1 2".
  • Hql — The format of HQL's own value notation: {a: 1, b: [true]} | hql is "{a: 1, b: [true]}".
  • Markdown — The Markdown format: read, the whole input is one String; written, a collection is a list, one item per element: [1, 2] | markdown is "- 1 - 2".
  • Hmd — The HyperMarkDown format, a narrowing of Markdown: every HyperMarkDown text is Markdown, and a value is written in it as in Markdown.
  • Json — The JSON format: read, each document is one Data value; written, a value is one indented JSON document.
  • JsonLines — The JSON Lines format, one JSON document per line: read, each line is one Data value; written, each element of a collection is one line of compact JSON: [{a: 1}, {a: 2}] | jsonlines is "{"a":1} {"a":2}".
  • Yaml — The YAML format: read, each document of the input, --- separating them, is one Data value; written, a value is one YAML document.
  • Csv — The comma-separated values format, with a header row: read, each row is one Data value whose fields, named by the header, hold Strings; written, a collection of records or a Table is the header and one row per element.
  • D2 — The D2 diagram format, which writes a Graph, or a Data value holding one, and nothing else.
  • Mermaid — The Mermaid diagram format, which writes a Graph, or a Data value holding one, and nothing else.
  • DiagnosticText — The text form of a Diagnostic (HQL-0045), which writes a diagnostic, or a sequence of them, and nothing else: each one's heading, phase severity[kind]: message, its origin and the fields that apply, then a count per severity when there is more than one.
  • Table — Rows of type R under ordered columns: the shape every format's encoder writes as a table.
  • Decoder — The contract that a format's records are read as values of T: source(e, F) gives the T of F's decoder.
  • Encoder — The contract that values of T are written as records of a format: format(x, F) takes the types F's encoders cover.
  • format — The formats, how bytes are read as values and how values are written as text, and the codec contracts over them.
  • text — x encoded as Text: x | text is format(x, Text).
  • hql — x encoded as Hql: x | hql is format(x, Hql).
  • markdown — x encoded as Markdown: x | markdown is format(x, Markdown).
  • hmd — x encoded as Hmd: x | hmd is format(x, Hmd).
  • json — x encoded as Json: x | json is format(x, Json).
  • yaml — x encoded as Yaml: x | yaml is format(x, Yaml).
  • csv — x encoded as Csv: x | csv is format(x, Csv).
  • lines — x encoded as Lines: x | lines is format(x, Lines).
  • jsonlines — x encoded as JsonLines: x | jsonlines is format(x, JsonLines).
  • d2 — x encoded as D2: x | d2 is format(x, D2).
  • mermaid — x encoded as Mermaid: x | mermaid is format(x, Mermaid).

module graph

Graphs: nodes and the edges among them, structural only; what a node or an edge means is the knowledge module's. There is no Node type: what a node is arrives as a type parameter, so a graph over documents and a graph over concepts share one declaration.

  • Edge — An edge from source to target, with data about it.
  • Graph — A graph: the set of its nodes, which are cards, and the set of its edges, the links among them.
  • Link — An authored link from one document to another: an Edge between cards.
  • HmdGraph — The document graph: a Graph of cards and the authored Links among them.
  • uplinks — The edges of the links x writes to other cards: one Edge per authored link, its source the card x.
  • downlinks — The edges of the links other cards of the vault write to x: one Edge per authored link, its target the card x.
  • expand — The graph reached from x by following links depth steps, 1 unless given, in direction: "uplinks", "downlinks" or "both", the default.

docs.title: std/io
docs.text:
module io

Input and output: endpoints, the data sources read from them, and the data targets written to them. An endpoint names where bytes are and performs no I/O; a format type (module format) states how the bytes are documents; a source or target joins the two, and Seq and Stream state whether the documents end.

  • Endpoint — The abstract type of every endpoint: where bytes are.
  • Readable — An endpoint bytes can be read from, by source and tap.
  • Replayable — A Readable endpoint that gives the same bytes on every read in one evaluation, so source reads what it holds as a Seq.
  • Writable — An endpoint bytes can be written to, by target and sink.
  • Transport — An endpoint outside the evaluation: a file, a process stream, a network resource, a database table or a broker's log.
  • Direct — A Transport on this machine: a process stream or the file system.
  • Network — A Transport in another process, reached over a connection.
  • ByteTransport — A Transport that moves bytes: a format separates the documents.
  • MessageTransport — A Transport that moves framed messages: each message is one document, decoded by the format, Json where none is named.
  • RowTransport — A Transport that moves rows of named columns: it takes no format.
  • Transactional — A Transport whose system has an atomic scope: statements over it begin, commit and roll back as one unit.
  • Insertable — A Transport that takes rows it does not hold, by insert.
  • Updatable — A Transport whose held rows a statement changes in place, by update.
  • Deletable — A Transport whose held rows a statement removes, by delete.
  • IsolationLevel — How much of other transactions a scope sees.
  • ReadCommitted — The IsolationLevel at which a statement sees what was committed before it began: PostgreSQL's default.
  • RepeatableRead — The IsolationLevel at which every statement of a scope sees the snapshot its first statement saw.
  • Serializable — The IsolationLevel at which concurrent scopes behave as if run one after another: SQLite's only level.
  • Transaction — The handle of a transaction scope, bound by with transaction tx on … (HQL-0051).
  • TransactionFailure — Why a transaction scope did not commit, the err of its Result: kind is "rolled_back" for tx.rollback, "conflict" for a concurrent transaction after the last attempt, "constraint" for a row the system refused, and "exhausted" for tx.retry with no attempt left; reason is the rollback argument or what the system said; attempts counts the attempts run.
  • Stdin — The program's standard input, bound as stdin: read once, as it arrives.
  • Stdout — The program's standard output, bound as stdout: written while the program runs, before the host presents its result.
  • Stderr — The program's standard error, bound as stderr: where diagnostics go, apart from the result.
  • FileEnd — The end of a file, after what it holds, as file(path).end: a write there appends, and tap follows what is written next, as tail -f does.
  • File — A local file, the whole of it: read, every document it holds; written, it is replaced.
  • Path — A place in a file system, written as text: segments separated by /.
  • Channel — An endpoint of values rather than bytes, held in memory for one execution scope: a program run, or one cell.
  • DataSource — What a program reads: a configured endpoint by id, or an endpoint read in a format.
  • FiniteSource — A source of every document, in order, that ends: read from a Replayable endpoint.
  • LiveSource — A source of each document as it arrives, with no replay: read from a live endpoint.
  • KeyedSource — A finite source whose contents are addressable by a key of type K.
  • Position — A message's place in its log, ordered as the log is.
  • Message — One element of a stream with where and when it sits in it: its value, its position, an optional key and time, and its headers.
  • StreamSource — A log: Message<T>s in order, replayable within its retention.
  • Catalog — An endpoint that contains sources of type S: a database of tables, a cluster of topics.
  • VaultSource — A vault as a source: an endpoint that holds its cards, as a catalog holds tables, with its members as fields rather than names.
  • DataTarget — What a program writes to: an endpoint written in a format, or a configured endpoint by its id.
  • file — The File at path.
  • join — self with segment appended as its last segment, separated by /: Path("data").join("birds.csv") is Path("data/birds.csv").
  • parent — self without its last segment, some(Path), or none for a path of one segment: Path("a/b").parent() is some(Path("a")), and Path("a").parent() is none.
  • name — The last segment of self: Path("data/birds.csv").name() is "birds.csv".
  • stem — The last segment of self without its extension: Path("data/birds.csv").stem() is "birds".
  • extension — The text after the last . of the last segment, some(String), or none where the segment has none: Path("a/b.csv").extension() is some("csv").
  • configured — The endpoint configured under the literal id in hql.toml, as the transport its kind states, with its schema boundary: a postgres endpoint is a Postgres, a csv endpoint a File.
  • source — Every document read from endpoint in format, decoded to T: a Seq from a Replayable endpoint, a Stream from a live one.
  • tap — The documents read from endpoint in format, one held at a time, as a Stream<T>.
  • target — Writes value as one document to endpoint in format, or to the target configured under id, and gives Step.
  • sink — Writes each of values to endpoint in format, one document per value, and gives Step: [{a: 1}, {a: 2}] | sink(stdout, Json) writes {"a":1} and {"a":2} on two lines.

effectful fn sink<T, F : Format>(values: Iterable<T>, endpoint: Writable, format: Type<F>) : Step

Writes each of values to endpoint in format, one document per value, and gives Step: [{a: 1}, {a: 2}] | sink(stdout, Json) writes {"a":1} and {"a":2} on two lines. Written to a Channel<T>, each value is appended and no format is taken. sink(id) writes to the target configured under id as each value arrives: a kafka topic or a nats or nats_jetstream subject takes one message per value, a postgres or a spark table one row per value of a declared record. Effectful: it runs once, where it is written.

Every document read from endpoint in format, decoded to T: a Seq from a Replayable endpoint, a Stream from a live one. T is the type the format decodes to, or the element type the read is expected to give: s : Seq<Sighting> = source(file("birds.json")) decodes each document as a Sighting. The format may be omitted when the endpoint is file of a literal path whose extension implies one. source(id) reads the source configured under the literal id in hql.toml, as the type its kind states, and takes no format; source(c) of a Channel<T> is a Seq<T> of what it holds now. docs.title: std/io/db/postgres
docs.text:
module io.db.postgres

PostgreSQL: one table of a database, as a transport read by source and tap and written by target like any other endpoint (module io). The postgres kind of a configured endpoint is this transport under an id, with a schema boundary. A program imports the module: import io.db.postgres.

  • Postgres — One table of a PostgreSQL database.
  • postgres — The table table of the database whose connection string the environment variable dsn_env holds, as a Postgres transport; its parameters are the keys of the postgres kind, each written by name.

docs.title: postgres
docs.text:
In std/io/db/postgres.

fn postgres(*, dsn_env: String, table: String, order: List<String> = []) : Postgres

The table table of the database whose connection string the environment variable dsn_env holds, as a Postgres transport; its parameters are the keys of the postgres kind, each written by name. A connection string may hold a password, so a program names the variable and never the string. table is schema-qualified where it holds a dot, audit.events. Rows are read in the order of the columns order names, and as the table is scanned without them. Constructing it opens no connection.

A constructed table has no schema boundary: a row is read as Data, or as the type an annotation names, and a declared record is written a column per field, the table's rows replaced. Its columns, mode and strictness are configured on a postgres endpoint.

docs.title: Postgres
docs.text:
In std/io/db/postgres.

type Postgres : {Network, RowTransport, Replayable, Writable, Transactional, Insertable, Updatable, Deletable}

One table of a PostgreSQL database. It is on the network and carries rows of named columns, so it takes no format. A table ends and reads the same rows each time in one evaluation, so it is Replayable: read, it is a Seq, a row per element. The database is one atomic scope over every table it holds, and a table's rows are inserted, changed and removed in place (HQL-0051).

Spark SQL: one table behind a Spark SQL endpoint, a Databricks SQL warehouse or a Spark Thrift Server, as a transport read by source and tap and written by target like any other endpoint (module io). The spark kind of a configured endpoint is this transport under an id, with a schema boundary. A program imports the module: import io.db.spark.

  • Spark — One table behind a Spark SQL endpoint.
  • spark — The table table, qualified by catalog and schema where it holds dots, behind the Spark SQL endpoint at url or at the address the environment variable url_env holds, one of the two, as a Spark transport; its parameters are the keys of the spark kind, each written by name.

docs.text:
In std/io/db/spark.

fn spark(*, table: String, url: String = "", url_env: String = "", token_env: String = "", order: List<String> = []) : Spark

The table table, qualified by catalog and schema where it holds dots, behind the Spark SQL endpoint at url or at the address the environment variable url_env holds, one of the two, as a Spark transport; its parameters are the keys of the spark kind, each written by name. token_env names the variable holding an access token, where the endpoint asks for one. Rows are read in the order of the columns order names, and as the table is scanned without them. Constructing it opens no session.

A constructed table has no schema boundary: a row is read as Data, or as the type an annotation names, and a declared record is written a column per field, the table's rows replaced. Its columns, mode and strictness are configured on a spark endpoint.

docs.title: Spark
docs.text:
In std/io/db/spark.

type Spark : {Network, RowTransport, Replayable, Writable, Transactional, Insertable, Updatable, Deletable}

One table behind a Spark SQL endpoint. It is on the network and carries rows of named columns, so it takes no format. A table ends and reads the same rows each time in one evaluation, so it is Replayable: read, it is a Seq, a row per element. A Delta table commits one statement atomically, so a transaction scope over it holds this one table and at most one statement; its rows are inserted, changed and removed in place where the table's format allows it (HQL-0051).

  • Sqlite — One table of an SQLite database file.
  • sqlite — The table table of the database file at path, as a Sqlite transport; its parameters are the keys of the sqlite kind.

docs.text:
In std/io/db/sqlite.

fn sqlite(path: String, table: String, order: List<String> = []) : Sqlite

The table table of the database file at path, as a Sqlite transport; its parameters are the keys of the sqlite kind. A relative path resolves as a file's does. Rows are read in the order of the columns order names, and in rowid order without them. Constructing it opens nothing.

A constructed table has no schema boundary: a row is read as Data, or as the type an annotation names, and a declared record is written a column per field, the table replaced. Its columns, mode and strictness are configured on a sqlite endpoint.

docs.title: Sqlite
docs.text:
In std/io/db/sqlite.

type Sqlite : {Direct, RowTransport, Replayable, Writable, Transactional, Insertable, Updatable, Deletable}

One table of an SQLite database file. It is on this machine and carries rows of named columns, so it takes no format. A table ends and reads the same rows each time in one evaluation, so it is Replayable: read, it is a Seq, a row per element. The database file is one atomic scope over every table it holds, and a table's rows are inserted, changed and removed in place (HQL-0051).

docs.text:
module io.env

What a program reads from the invocation that runs it: environment variables and named arguments. The environment is read through a grant: a program run alone is granted every variable; a workspace's hql.toml narrows the grant to env = ["NAME", "PREFIX_*"], a * matching any suffix; hql render grants none. A variable that is unset, withheld by the grant, or whose value is not UTF-8 reads as absent, and the three are indistinguishable. Arguments are the --arg name=value pairs of the invocation, always granted. Each operation reads a value fixed for the whole evaluation. A program imports the module, import io.env, and reaches it as env.

  • var — The value of the environment variable name, or none where it is unset, withheld by the grant, or not UTF-8: env.var("API_TOKEN") | unwrap_or("").
  • vars — Every granted environment variable that is set and UTF-8, by name.
  • arg — The value of the invocation's --arg name=value, or none where no --arg names it.
  • args — Every --arg name=value of the invocation, by name.

docs.title: std/io/fs
docs.text:
module io.fs

The file system as data: folders, globs over paths, and the entries a folder holds, with their kinds, sizes and modification times. Constructing a Folder or a Glob opens, stats and resolves nothing; the listing operations read the file system, each once, where it is written, and give a Seq<Entry> in the order of a sorted walk, never the file system's. A listing is granted exactly where reading a file at the same path is. A program imports the module: import io.fs, and reaches it as fs.

  • Folder — A folder of the file system at path: an endpoint that holds files and folders, as a database holds tables.
  • Glob — A pattern over paths, matched against a path relative to the folder it is applied to: * matches within one segment, ** any number of whole segments, ? one character other than /, and [abc] one character of the set, [a-z] one of the range.
  • Entry — One thing a folder holds: its path, the listed folder's path joined with the entry's path below it, so file(e.path) reads it; its name, the last segment; its kind, "file", "folder" or "link"; its size, a file's length in bytes, absent for a folder or a link; and its modified, the time the entry was last modified, a link's own and not its target's, absent where the platform does not record one.
  • folder — The Folder at path, a String or a Path.
  • matches — Whether path, read as relative to the folder the glob is applied to, matches self.
  • entries — The entries directly in self, sorted by name, an entry whose name opens with . included.
  • walk — Every entry below self, the folder itself excluded: depth first, each folder's entries sorted by name, and each folder followed at once by what it holds.
  • glob — The entries of walk(self) whose path below self matches pattern, in walk order.
  • exists — Whether something is at self: a file, a folder or a link.
  • entry — The Entry at self, some(Entry), or none where nothing is there.

Every entry below self, the folder itself excluded: depth first, each folder's entries sorted by name, and each folder followed at once by what it holds. This is the sorted walk a vault reads its cards in; the vault skips the entries whose name opens with ., and walk lists them.

docs.title: std/io/logging
docs.text:
module io.logging

Logging: structured events written to a destination, apart from the result. A logger owns no writer: it names a producer and holds a destination, as sink would write it (module io): stderr or a file in a format, a network endpoint, or a Channel<LogEvent> that keeps the events as values for the host. A program imports the module: import logging.

  • LogLevel — How severe an event is.
  • Trace — The least severe LogLevel, below Debug.
  • Debug — The LogLevel above Trace and below Info.
  • Info — The LogLevel above Debug and below Warn; a logger's threshold unless written.
  • Warn — The LogLevel above Info and below Error.
  • Error — The most severe LogLevel, above Warn.
  • LogEvent — One logged event: its level, the logger that produced it, its message and its data.
  • Logger — A producer of events: its name and the least severe level it writes.
  • trace — Writes one Trace event with message and data to log's destination when log's threshold is Trace, and gives Step.
  • debug — Writes one Debug event with message and data to log's destination when log's threshold is at most Debug, and gives Step.
  • info — Writes one Info event with message and data to log's destination when log's threshold is at most Info, and gives Step.
  • warn — Writes one Warn event with message and data to log's destination when log's threshold is at most Warn, and gives Step.
  • error — Writes one Error event with message and data to log's destination, whatever log's threshold, and gives Step.
  • Cell — The cell hql render is running, bound as cell.

docs.title: debug
docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

effectful fn debug(log: Logger, message: String, data: Data = {:}) : Step

Writes one Debug event with message and data to log's destination when log's threshold is at most Debug, and gives Step. Effectful: log | debug("parsed", {rows: 3}).

docs.title: error
docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

effectful fn error(log: Logger, message: String, data: Data = {:}) : Step

Writes one Error event with message and data to log's destination, whatever log's threshold, and gives Step. Effectful: log | error("unreadable", {path: "birds.json"}).

docs.title: info
docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

effectful fn info(log: Logger, message: String, data: Data = {:}) : Step

Writes one Info event with message and data to log's destination when log's threshold is at most Info, and gives Step. Effectful: with log = Logger(stdout, Text, name = "birds"), log | info("loaded", {count: 312}) writes INFO birds loaded {count: 312}.

docs.title: trace
docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

effectful fn trace(log: Logger, message: String, data: Data = {:}) : Step

Writes one Trace event with message and data to log's destination when log's threshold is Trace, and gives Step. Effectful. Called directly or through a pipe: trace(log, "step") is log | trace("step").

docs.title: warn
docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

effectful fn warn(log: Logger, message: String, data: Data = {:}) : Step

Writes one Warn event with message and data to log's destination when log's threshold is at most Warn, and gives Step. Effectful: log | warn("no sightings").

docs.title: Cell
docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

type Cell { logs : Channel<LogEvent> }

The cell hql render is running, bound as cell. The events written to its logs are shown beside the cell's result and never saved into the document.

docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

type Debug : LogLevel

The LogLevel above Trace and below Info.

docs.title: Error
docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

type Error : LogLevel

The most severe LogLevel, above Warn.

docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

type Info : LogLevel

The LogLevel above Debug and below Warn; a logger's threshold unless written.

docs.title: LogEvent
docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

type LogEvent { level : LogLevel logger : String // the producer's name, dotted by convention: hql.query message : String data : Data // structured context, {:} when none is given }

One logged event: its level, the logger that produced it, its message and its data. Written as Text it is one line, the level, the logger and the message, then the data as an HQL literal unless it is empty:

INFO birds loaded {count: 312}

Written as Json it is one document with these four keys.

docs.title: LogLevel
docs.text:
In std/io/logging.

abstract type LogLevel

How severe an event is. The five levels are ordered from least to most severe: Trace, Debug, Info, Warn, Error. A level is tested with e.level | is(Error), and a threshold is passed as a type: level = Info.

docs.text:

type Logger { name : String level : LogLevel // the least severe level it writes }

A producer of events: its name and the least severe level it writes. Its destination is not a field: what a logger writes to is visible only where it is constructed.

fn Logger<F : Format, L : LogLevel>(to: Writable, format: Type<F>, *, name: String, level: Type<L> = Info) : Logger

A Logger named name that writes to to in format each event at least as severe as level, Info unless written. The format is omitted for a Channel<LogEvent>, which takes the events as values. Construction is pure and writes nothing: Logger(stderr, Text, name = "birds").

docs.title: std/io/msg/nats
docs.text:
module io.msg.nats

Core NATS: one subject, as a transport read by tap and written by sink and target like any other endpoint (module io). The server keeps nothing: a read is given what is published while it is subscribed, and a message published while no one is subscribed reaches no one. A stream that keeps a subject's messages is io.msg.nats_jetstream. The nats kind of a configured endpoint is this transport under an id. A program imports the module: import io.msg.nats.

  • Nats — One core NATS subject on a server.
  • nats — The subject subject, as a Nats transport; its parameters are the keys of the nats kind.

docs.title: nats
docs.text:
In std/io/msg/nats.

fn nats(subject: String, url: String = "", url_env: String = "", idle_ms: Int = 0) : Nats

The subject subject, as a Nats transport; its parameters are the keys of the nats kind. A read may name wildcards, * for one token and > for every token after it; a write names one subject. The server's address is url, or the value of the environment variable url_env names, one of the two; an address that holds credentials is named by url_env. A read ends once no message has arrived for idle_ms milliseconds, or never when that is 0. Constructing it opens no connection.

docs.title: Nats
docs.text:
In std/io/msg/nats.

type Nats : {Network, MessageTransport, Readable, Writable}

One core NATS subject on a server. It is on the network and carries messages, each one document, Json unless a format is named. It is Readable and not Replayable: read, it is a Stream.

docs.title: std/io/msg/nats_jetstream
docs.text:
module io.msg.nats_jetstream

NATS JetStream: one subject of a stream, as a transport read by tap and written by sink and target like any other endpoint (module io). A stream keeps what is published to its subjects, so a read starts where it says, and a message is written once the stream acknowledges it. The nats_jetstream kind of a configured endpoint is this transport under an id. A program imports the module: import io.msg.nats_jetstream.

  • NatsJetStream — One subject of a JetStream stream on a NATS server.
  • nats_jetstream — The subject subject of the stream stream, as a NatsJetStream transport; its parameters are the keys of the nats_jetstream kind.

docs.title: nats_jetstream
docs.text:
In std/io/msg/nats_jetstream.

fn nats_jetstream(subject: String, stream: String, url: String = "", url_env: String = "", from: String = "earliest", idle_ms: Int = 0, consumer: String = "") : NatsJetStream

The subject subject of the stream stream, as a NatsJetStream transport; its parameters are the keys of the nats_jetstream kind. The server's address is url, or the value of the environment variable url_env names, one of the two; an address that holds credentials is named by url_env. A read starts at the "earliest" message the stream keeps, or at the next one published under from = "latest", and ends once no message has arrived for idle_ms milliseconds, or never when that is 0. With consumer, the server keeps the read's position under that name, so a later read starts after the last message acknowledged. Constructing it opens no connection.

docs.title: NatsJetStream
docs.text:
In std/io/msg/nats_jetstream.

type NatsJetStream : {Network, MessageTransport, Readable, Writable}

One subject of a JetStream stream on a NATS server. It is on the network and carries messages, each one document, Json unless a format is named. A stream is a log that does not end, so it is Readable and not Replayable: read, it is a Stream.

docs.title: std/io/net
docs.text:
module io.net

Network endpoints: transports, read and written by source, tap, target and sink like any other endpoint (module io). Constructing one sends nothing: the request a program describes happens when a source, tap, target or sink uses it, and only if the host grants the network to that program. A document reaches no network. A program imports the module: import net.

  • Http — An HTTP resource at url.
  • WebSocket — A WebSocket connection to url: each message is a document, read as it arrives and written as it is sent.
  • Tcp — A TCP connection to host on port.
  • http — The HTTP resource at url, as an Http endpoint: method is the request a write sends, "GET" unless given, and headers a map of header names to values sent with every request.
  • websocket — The WebSocket at url, as a WebSocket endpoint.
  • tcp — The TCP endpoint host on port, as a Tcp.

docs.title: http
docs.text:
In std/io/net.

fn http(url: String, method: String = "GET", headers: Data = {:}, timeout_ms: Int = 30000) : Http

The HTTP resource at url, as an Http endpoint: method is the request a write sends, "GET" unless given, and headers a map of header names to values sent with every request. A response that sends nothing for timeout_ms milliseconds fails, naming the URL; the bound is 30 seconds unless given, and a given one is above 0. Constructing it sends nothing.

docs.title: tcp
docs.text:
In std/io/net.

fn tcp(host: String, port: Int) : Tcp

The TCP endpoint host on port, as a Tcp. Constructing it opens no connection.

docs.title: websocket
docs.text:
In std/io/net.

fn websocket(url: String) : WebSocket

The WebSocket at url, as a WebSocket endpoint. Constructing it opens no connection.

docs.title: Http
docs.text:
In std/io/net.

type Http : {Replayable, Writable} { url : String method : String // "GET" unless written headers : Data // a map of header names to values }

An HTTP resource at url. Read, it is a GET whose response body is its bytes; the host reads it once per evaluation, so it is Replayable. Written, it is a request by method whose body is the document, and the response is not read beyond its status. Both send headers, a map of header names to values. Authentication belongs in a configured endpoint, not in the program. A connection not made within 10 seconds fails, and so does a response that sends nothing for 30 seconds, or for the timeout_ms given; each failure names the URL.

docs.title: Tcp
docs.text:
In std/io/net.

type Tcp : {Readable, Writable} { host : String port : Int }

A TCP connection to host on port. A TCP stream carries bytes, not messages, so the documents on it are separated as their format separates them: whitespace between Json values, a line for Lines, JsonLines and Csv, a --- line for Yaml. A connection not made within 10 seconds fails, naming the address; a read waits for the next document without limit.

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text:
In std/io/net.

type WebSocket : {Readable, Writable} { url : String }

A WebSocket connection to url: each message is a document, read as it arrives and written as it is sent. A connection not made within 10 seconds fails, and so does a handshake the server answers nothing to for 30 seconds, naming the URL; once open, a read waits for the next message without limit.

docs.title: std/io/transaction
docs.text:
module io.transaction for Transaction

The control calls of a transaction scope's handle, tx, bound by with transaction tx on participants { … } (module io): each ends the attempt and gives no value, so it stands where any type is expected and nothing after it runs. A block that reaches its end commits with its final value, so a scope needs none of them. In the prelude.

  • commit — Ends the attempt by committing it, with value as the scope's ok.
  • rollback — Ends the attempt by rolling it back, with reason in the scope's err, its kind "rolled_back".
  • retry — Ends the attempt by rolling it back and runs the block again on a fresh transaction, as the next attempt, while the scope's attempts remain; with none remaining the scope's err has the kind "exhausted".

docs.title: commit
docs.text:
In std/io/transaction.

effectful fn commit<T>(self, value: T) : Never

Ends the attempt by committing it, with value as the scope's ok. Written only to commit before the end of the block: tx.commit(0) given nothing_to_do.

docs.title: retry
docs.text:
In std/io/transaction.

effectful fn retry(self) : Never

Ends the attempt by rolling it back and runs the block again on a fresh transaction, as the next attempt, while the scope's attempts remain; with none remaining the scope's err has the kind "exhausted".

docs.text:
In std/io/transaction.

effectful fn rollback(self, reason: String) : Never

Ends the attempt by rolling it back, with reason in the scope's err, its kind "rolled_back". Nothing the attempt wrote to a participant remains: tx.rollback("insufficient balance") given sender.balance < 100.

The channel named name in the current scope, holding T. The element type is written at the call, Channel<LogEvent>("logs"), since nothing written to the channel yet determines it.

docs.text:

The abstract type of every endpoint: where bytes are. Constructing one opens, stats and resolves nothing.

In std/io.

type File : {Replayable, Writable} { path : String end : FileEnd // file(p).end appends, and tap(file(p).end, F) follows }

How much of other transactions a scope sees. The three levels are SQL's, from least to most isolated. A kind offers a subset, and a level is passed as a type, isolation = Serializable.

docs.title: KeyedSource

A Transport that moves framed messages: each message is one document, decoded by the format, Json where none is named.

docs.title: Network

abstract type Network : Transport

A Transport in another process, reached over a connection. A host grants or refuses the network as a whole.

type Path : Orderable { text : String }

A place in a file system, written as text: segments separated by /. Constructing one touches nothing. A relative path resolves against the directory of the source unit that names it, as a file's does. Paths are ordered by their segments compared in turn, each by its text, so Path("a/b") sorts before Path("a-b"): the order of a sorted walk.

A message's place in its log, ordered as the log is.

docs.title: Stderr

docs.title: StreamSource
docs.text:

docs.title: Transaction
docs.text:
In std/io.

type Transaction

The handle of a transaction scope, bound by with transaction tx on … (HQL-0051). It has no fields and no constructor. It is used in its own block, through tx.commit(value), tx.rollback(reason) and tx.retry() (module io.transaction), and does not leave it: it is not a parameter, a field, an element or a result, as a Window is not.

docs.title: TransactionFailure
docs.text:
In std/io.

type TransactionFailure : DataContract { kind : String reason : String attempts : Int endpoint? : String detail? : Data }

Why a transaction scope did not commit, the err of its Result: kind is "rolled_back" for tx.rollback, "conflict" for a concurrent transaction after the last attempt, "constraint" for a row the system refused, and "exhausted" for tx.retry with no attempt left; reason is the rollback argument or what the system said; attempts counts the attempts run. endpoint and detail are declared for the participant and the system's state code, and are absent today: no backend reports them yet, and what the system said is in reason.

module knowledge

Knowledge: the semantic domain, where everything is a claim. Every declaration is a type; the module declares no operation.

  • Concept — Something identified or described: the type that puts a card in a node position.
  • Proposition — A claim that can be supported, disputed or constrained.
  • Evidence — Material offered for or against a claim.

docs.text:
module math

Numbers, in the prelude. abs, pow and sign take an Int or a Float, abs and sign a Decimal too, and abs a Duration; round takes a Float or a Decimal, and the rest take a Float. float, int and decimal convert between the three, since no number widens on its own except an Int beside a Decimal.

  • abs — self without its sign, at its own type: abs(-3) is 3, abs(-1.50) is 1.50, and abs(Duration("-PT1H")) is PT1H.
  • pow — self raised to exponent, both of one type: pow(2, 10) is 1024.
  • sign — -1, 0 or 1 by the sign of self, as an Int: sign(-0.5) is -1.
  • float — self as a Float, the Float nearest it: float(1.10) is 1.1.
  • int — The integer part of self, as an Int, the fraction dropped toward zero: int(-2.9f) is -2.
  • decimal — self as a Decimal: an Int exactly, and a Float by the shortest digits that read back as it: decimal(0.1f) is 0.1.
  • gcd — The greatest common divisor of self and other, at least 0: gcd(12, 18) is 6, and gcd(0, 0) is 0.
  • sqrt — The square root of self: sqrt(2.0f) is 1.4142135623730951.
  • floor — The greatest whole number not above self, as a Float: floor(-1.5f) is -2.0.
  • ceil — The least whole number not below self, as a Float: ceil(-1.5f) is -1.0.
  • round — The whole number nearest self, as a Float; a value halfway between two rounds away from zero: 2.5f | round is 3.0.
  • exp — e raised to self: exp(1.0f) is 2.718281828459045.
  • ln — The natural logarithm of self: ln(1.0f) is 0.0.
  • log10 — The base-10 logarithm of self: log10(1000.0f) is 3.0.
  • sin — The sine of self, an angle in radians: sin(0.0f) is 0.0.
  • cos — The cosine of self, an angle in radians: cos(0.0f) is 1.0.
  • tan — The tangent of self, an angle in radians: tan(0.0f) is 0.0.

module option for Option<T>

docs.title: std/random
docs.text:
module random

Randomness: samples, shuffles, choices, numbers and UUIDs. Each draw has two forms. With a seed argument it is pure: its result is a function of the seed, its input and its call site. Without one it is effectful and draws from the evaluation seed, fixed once per evaluation from the host's entropy or --seed. The generator is ChaCha12 and is not fit for keys, tokens or any other secret: a seeded draw is predictable by design. Not in the prelude: a program writes import random.

  • sample — n elements of self drawn without replacement, in their order in self; all of self where n is not below its size.
  • shuffle — The elements of self in a uniformly random order (Fisher–Yates).
  • choice — One element of self drawn uniformly, or none where self is empty.
  • random_int — An Int drawn uniformly from low to high, both included.
  • random_float — A Float drawn uniformly from 0.0 included to 1.0 excluded.
  • uuid — A version 7 UUID: its first 48 bits are the evaluation instant's Unix milliseconds and the next 42 a counter, so the UUIDs of one evaluation sort in the order they were drawn.

docs.text:
module regex

Text matched against a regular expression. A pattern is a String; one that does not parse is an evaluation error at the call. The module is imported where it is used: import regex.

  • is_match — Whether pattern matches somewhere in text: "a1b22c" | regex.is_match("[0-9]+") is true.
  • find — The first match of pattern in text, or none: "a1b22c" | regex.find("[0-9]+") is "1".
  • find_all — Every non-overlapping match of pattern in text, in order: "a1b22c" | regex.find_all("[0-9]+") is ["1", "22"].
  • captures — The first match of pattern in text and its groups, whole match first, or none; a group that took no part in the match is "": "a" | regex.captures("(a)|(b)") is ["a", "a", ""].
  • replace_all — text with every match of pattern replaced by replacement, in which $1 is the first group: "a1b22c" | regex.replace_all("([0-9]+)", "<$1>") is "a<1>b<22>c".
  • replace_first — text with the first match of pattern replaced by replacement, in which $1 is the first group: "a1b22c" | regex.replace_first("[0-9]+", "#") is "a#b22c".
  • split — The pieces of text between matches of pattern, in order: "a1b22c" | regex.split("[0-9]+") is ["a", "b", "c"].

module result for Result<T, E>

The ways out of a Result<T, E>, in the prelude, each stating what a failure gives. A result is ok(v) or err(e). There is no unwrap. map over a result is the core's step applied to the value of a success: ok(3) | map(n => n + 1) is ok(4).

  • is_ok — Whether self is a success: ok(4) | is_ok is true.
  • is_err — Whether self is a failure: err("x") | is_err is true.
  • ok — The value of self when a success, and none when a failure: err("x") | ok is none.
  • err — The error of self when a failure, and none when a success: ok(4) | err is none.
  • unwrap_or — The value of self when a success, and default when a failure: err("x") | unwrap_or(0) is 0.
  • unwrap_or_else — The value of self when a success, and default applied to the error when a failure: err("ab") | unwrap_or_else(e => e.size()) is 2.
  • map_err — A failure with by applied to its error; a success is kept as it is: err("x") | map_err(e => e.upper()) is err("X").
  • and_then — by applied to the value of a success, its own failure kept; a failure is kept as it is: ok(4) | and_then(n => ok(n * 2)) is ok(8).
  • or_else — by applied to the error of a failure, giving another result; a success is kept as it is: err("x") | or_else(e => ok(e.size())) is ok(1).

  • Hit — One ranked value: the value, its score against query, and the retrieval that produced it, a tree holding index, model, revision, metric, approximate and query.
  • Ranking — The hits of one retrieval, as a Seq<Hit<T>> in descending order of score, ties ordered by name, with the query they are relative to and the retrieval that produced them.

docs.title: std/seq
docs.text:
module seq for Seq<T> : Index<T>, Slice

The sequence, set and map operations beyond the core's membership, order and lookup, in the prelude. A receiver module over Seq<T>, with T bound per call; a function that takes any collection writes its receiver, self: Collection<T>, and the functions over sets and maps take theirs as a typed first parameter. A receiver S : Seq<T> comes back at its own type, and F<_> : Seq<_> rebuilt in its own constructor. Every sequence implements Index<T> and Slice through at and slice: xs[i] is xs.at(i), and xs[a:b] is xs.slice(Range(start = a, end = b)).

  • at — The element of self at position, or none past either end; a negative position counts from the end: [3, 1, 2].at(1) and [3, 1, 2][1] are 1.
  • slice — The elements of self within range, clamped to the sequence, a negative bound counting from the end: [1, 2, 3][1:] is [2, 3].
  • first — The element at position 0, or none over an empty sequence: [3, 1, 2] | first is 3.
  • one — The one element of self: a sequence of exactly one.
  • last — The element at the last position, or none over an empty sequence: [3, 1, 2] | last is 2.
  • reverse — The elements of self in the opposite order, in its own constructor: [1, 2, 3] | reverse is [3, 2, 1].
  • distinct — Each value of self once, at its first position, at the type of self: [1, 2, 1, 3, 2] | distinct is [1, 2, 3].
  • zip — Pairs of the elements of self and other at equal positions, as long as the shorter: [1, 2, 3] | zip(["a", "b"]) is [Pair(first = 1, second = "a"), Pair(first = 2, second = "b")].
  • enumerate — Each element of self paired with its position, counting from 0: ["a", "b"] | enumerate is [Pair(first = 0, second = "a"), Pair(first = 1, second = "b")].
  • any — Whether by holds of some value of self; false over an empty collection: [1, 2, 3] | any(x => x > 2) is true.
  • all — Whether by holds of every value of self; true over an empty collection: [] | all(x => x > 2) is true.
  • find — The first element of self that by accepts, or none: [1, 2, 3, 4] | find(x => x > 2) is 3.
  • position — The position of the first element of self that by accepts, counting from 0, or none: [1, 2, 3, 4] | position(x => x > 2) is 2.
  • take_while — The leading values of self that by accepts, up to the first it rejects: [1, 2, 5, 1] | take_while(x => x < 3) is [1, 2].
  • drop_while — The values of self after the leading ones by accepts, at the type of self: [1, 2, 5, 1] | drop_while(x => x < 3) is [5, 1].
  • window — Every run of n consecutive elements of self, in order: [1, 2, 3, 4] | window(2) is [[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4]].
  • partition — The values of self redistributed by the key by gives: each value once, at its own type, those of one key in one logical partition.
  • is_empty — Whether self has no values: [] | is_empty is true.
  • join — Every pair of a value of self and a value of other that by relates, in the order of self, then of other: [1, 2] | join([1, 2, 3], (a, b) => a < b) gives the pairs (1, 2), (1, 3) and (2, 3).
  • min_by — The value of self that is least, by the key by gives or by the Ordering by gives two values; the first of equals, or none over an empty collection: ["bb", "a", "ccc"] | min_by(s => size(s)) is "a".
  • max_by — The value of self that is greatest, by the key by gives or by the Ordering by gives two values; the first of equals, or none over an empty collection: ["bb", "a", "ccc"] | max_by(s => size(s)) is "ccc".
  • over — Each value of self, at its input position, as what into gives for it and its Window: the values with its key by, ordered by order, a key or a comparison.
  • row_number — The row's position in its ordered partition, from 1; no two rows share one.
  • rank — One more than the number of rows strictly before the row: rows equal under the order share it, and the next skips the shared positions.
  • dense_rank — The row's rank counting each set of equal rows once: rows equal under the order share it, and the next is one more.
  • lag — The row n positions before, or none before the first.
  • lead — The row n positions after, or none past the last.
  • running — The rows from the first up to and including the row, in order: SQL's ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
  • rows — The rows from before positions before the row to after positions after it, clipped to the partition.
  • whole — Every row of the partition, in order.
  • to_map — A map from the key of each value of self to its value; two values with one key are an evaluation error: ["bb", "a"] | to_map(s => s, s => size(s)) is Map {"bb": 2, "a": 1}.
  • range — The Ints from start up to, not including, end, each step after the one before: range(1, 6) is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], and range(10, 0, -3) is [10, 7, 4, 1].
  • with — The map self with key set to value, added or replaced, at the type of self: Map(["a"], [1]) | with("b", 2) is Map {"a": 1, "b": 2}.
  • without — The map self without key, whether or not it held it, at the type of self: Map(["a", "b"], [1, 2]) | without("a") is Map {"b": 2}.
  • entries — Each association of the map self as a Pair of its key and its value, in the map's order.
  • values — The values of the map self, in the map's order: Map(["b", "a"], [2, 1]) | values is [2, 1].
  • intersection — The members of both self and other, at the type of self: {1, 2, 3} | intersection({2, 3, 4}) is {2, 3}.
  • difference — The members of self that other does not hold, at the type of self: {1, 2, 3} | difference({2, 3, 4}) is {1}.

docs.title: std/stats
docs.text:
module stats

Descriptive statistics over a collection of numbers: the mean, the sample and population variance and standard deviation, the median, quantiles, the mode, covariance and correlation. A statistic of Int or Float values is a Float; a statistic of Decimal values is a Decimal, exact except where a quotient does not terminate, which is rounded half to even to 100 significant digits as Decimal / is. An Int statistic is computed exactly and rounded to a Float once. A statistic that is undefined over its input, the mean of nothing or the sample variance of one value, is none. Not in the prelude: a program writes import stats. The prelude's variance is the population variance of Int and Float values, so a program importing stats writes stats.variance for the sample variance of those.

  • mean — The arithmetic mean, the sum divided by the count, or none over an empty collection: [1, 2, 3, 4] | mean is 2.5.
  • variance — The sample variance, the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by n - 1, or none over fewer than two values: [1, 2, 3, 4] | stats.variance is 1.6666666666666667.
  • stdev — The sample standard deviation, the square root of variance, or none over fewer than two values.
  • pvariance — The population variance, the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by n, or none over an empty collection: [1, 2, 3, 4] | pvariance is 1.25.
  • pstdev — The population standard deviation, the square root of pvariance, or none over an empty collection.
  • covariance — The sample covariance of the pairs' first and second values, the sum of the products of their deviations from their means divided by n - 1, or none over fewer than two pairs.
  • correlation — Pearson's correlation coefficient of the pairs' first and second values, the covariance divided by the product of the two standard deviations, or none over fewer than two pairs or where either side has zero variance.
  • median — The middle value of the collection sorted ascending, the mean of the two middle values where the count is even; quantile(0.5).
  • quantile — The q quantile, by linear interpolation between the sorted values (Hyndman and Fan's type 7, the default of R and NumPy): with the values sorted as s_0 to s_(n-1) and h = (n - 1) * q, it is s_floor(h) + (h - floor(h)) * (s_(floor(h) + 1) - s_floor(h)).
  • quantiles — The n - 1 cut points that divide the sorted values into n groups of equal probability, the quantiles at 1/n to (n-1)/n by the same interpolation as quantile, each computed as (s_j * (n - d) + s_(j+1) * d) / n with one division.
  • mode — The most frequent value, and among equally frequent values the least by the type's order, or none over an empty collection: [3, 1, 3, 1, 2] | mode is 1.

docs.title: std/string
docs.text:
module string for String : Index<String>, Slice

The functions of a String, in the prelude. A receiver module: each function takes self, so s.trim(), string.trim(s) and s | trim are one declaration. A String is a sequence of Unicode scalar values held as UTF-8, whatever encoding its text was read from. Positions and size count code points. A String implements Index<String> and Slice through at and slice: s[1] is s.at(1), and s[1:3] is s.slice(Range(start = 1, end = 3)).

  • at — The character of self at position, as text, or none outside the text; a negative position counts from the end: "hello".at(1) and "hello"[1] are "e".
  • str — The text self prints as, for a value of any type: str(some(2)) is "2".
  • fmt — The template self with each {} replaced by the text of the next of args, in order: fmt("{} of {}", 1, some(2)) is "1 of 2".
  • size — How many characters self has, counting code points: "héllo" | size is 5, and s.size() == s.chars().size() for every s.
  • upper — self in upper case: "Straße" | upper is "STRASSE".
  • lower — self in lower case: "ÀB" | lower is "àb".
  • trim — self without leading and trailing whitespace: " a b " | trim is "a b".
  • trim_start — self without leading whitespace: " a " | trim_start is "a ".
  • trim_end — self without trailing whitespace: " a " | trim_end is " a".
  • capitalize — self with its first character in upper case: "élan" | capitalize is "Élan".
  • split — The pieces of self between occurrences of separator, in order: "a,b,,c" | split(",") is ["a", "b", "", "c"].
  • join — The texts of self in order, with separator between each two: ["a", "b"].join(", ") is "a, b".
  • replace_all — self with every occurrence of from replaced by to: "aaa" | replace_all("a", "b") is "bbb".
  • replace_first — self with the first occurrence of from replaced by to: "aaa" | replace_first("a", "b") is "baa".
  • starts_with — Whether self begins with part: "hello" | starts_with("he") is true.
  • ends_with — Whether self ends with part: "hello" | ends_with("lo") is true.
  • contains — Whether part occurs in self: "hello" | contains("ell") is true.
  • index_of — The position of the first occurrence of part in self, counting characters from 0, or none: "héllo" | index_of("l") is 2.
  • last_index_of — The position of the last occurrence of part in self, counting characters from 0, or none: "héllo" | last_index_of("l") is 3.
  • occurrences — How many non-overlapping times part occurs in self; 0 for an empty part: "aaaa" | occurrences("aa") is 2.
  • strip_prefix — self without part at its start, or none when it does not begin with it: "x.hql" | strip_prefix("x.") is "hql".
  • strip_suffix — self without part at its end, or none when it does not end with it: "x.hql" | strip_suffix(".hql") is "x".
  • trim_prefix — self without part at its start, or self as it is when it does not begin with it: "x" | trim_prefix("y") is "x".
  • trim_suffix — self without part at its end, or self as it is when it does not end with it: "x.hql" | trim_suffix(".hql") is "x".
  • equals_ignore_case — Whether self and other are equal in lower case: "ABC" | equals_ignore_case("abc") is true.
  • chars — Each character of self as its own text, in order: "héy" | chars is ["h", "é", "y"].
  • lines — The lines of self, without their line breaks; a final line break opens no empty line: string.lines("a\nb\n") is ["a", "b"].
  • words — The whitespace-separated words of self: " a b\tc " | words is ["a", "b", "c"].
  • reverse — The characters of self in the opposite order: "héllo" | reverse is "olléh".
  • repeat — self written times times in a row; "" for times below 1: "ab" | repeat(3) is "ababab".
  • pad_left — self preceded by fill, repeated, until it is width characters long; a longer self as it is: "7" | pad_left(3, "0") is "007".
  • pad_right — self followed by fill, repeated, until it is width characters long; a longer self as it is: "7" | pad_right(3, "0") is "700".
  • center — self between fills until it is width characters long; an odd fill character goes after it: "ab" | center(5, "*") is "*ab**".
  • truncate — At most the first width characters of self: "hello" | truncate(3) is "hel".
  • slice — The characters of self from start up to, not including, end, counting from 0; s[start:end].
  • char_at — The character of self at position, counting from 0, or none outside the text: "hello" | char_at(1) is "e".
  • to_int — The integer self writes, surrounding whitespace aside, or none when it writes none: "-42" | to_int is -42, and "1.5" | to_int is none.
  • to_float — The number self writes, as a Float, or none when it writes none: "1e3" | to_float is 1000.0.
  • to_decimal — The exact decimal number self writes, at its written scale, or none when it writes none: "2.50" | to_decimal is 2.50.
  • to_bool — The truth value self writes as true or false, or none for any other text: "True" | to_bool is none.
  • is_empty — Whether self has no characters: "" | is_empty is true.
  • is_blank — Whether self has no characters other than whitespace: " " | is_blank is true.
  • ord — The Unicode code point of the one-character text self, or none for any other text: "a" | ord is 97.
  • chr — The one-character text of the Unicode code point self, or none for an Int that is none: 97 | chr is "a".
  • bytes — The UTF-8 encoding of self, one Int per byte: "é" | bytes is [195, 169].
