docs.title: std/time
docs.text:
module time

Time: zones, the units a value truncates to, and the operations over the time scalars of core: conversion from text, parts, arithmetic, truncation, rendering, and the evaluation clock. Not in the prelude: a program writes import time.

  • Zone — A time zone: an IANA name the time-zone database holds, "Europe/Berlin", "UTC", or a fixed offset "+02:00".
  • TimeUnit — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Nanosecond — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Microsecond — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Millisecond — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Second — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Minute — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Hour — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Day — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Week — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Month — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Quarter — The units a time value truncates to.
  • Year — The units a time value truncates to.
  • to_date — self read as an ISO 8601 date, some(Date), or none where it is not one: "2026-10-24".to_date() is some(2026-10-24).
  • to_datetime — self read as an ISO 8601 date-time with no offset, or none.
  • to_instant — self read as an RFC 3339 instant, with Z or an offset, or none.
  • to_duration — self read as an ISO 8601 duration without years or months, or none.
  • parse_date — self read through a strftime pattern as a Date, or none where it does not match: "24.10.2026".parse_date("%d.%m.%Y").
  • parse_datetime — self read through a strftime pattern as a DateTime, or none.
  • parse_instant — self read through a strftime pattern as an Instant, or none; the pattern writes an offset with %z or a zone with %Z.
  • at — The wall-clock reading of self in zone.
  • in_zone — The instant the wall-clock reading self names in zone.
  • offset — The offset from UTC self has at the instant at: PT2H in Berlin in summer.
  • year — The year of self.
  • month — The month of self, 1..12.
  • day — The day of the month of self, 1..31.
  • weekday — The ISO day of the week of self: Monday is 1, Sunday is 7.
  • day_of_year — The day of the year of self, 1..366.
  • iso_week — The ISO week of self, 1..53, in the year iso_year gives.
  • iso_year — The year the ISO week of self belongs to: 2025 for 2024-12-30, the Monday of the first ISO week of 2025.
  • date — The date of self.
  • hour — The hour of self, 0..23.
  • minute — The minute of self, 0..59.
  • second — The second of self, 0..59.
  • nanosecond — The nanoseconds of self past its second.
  • unix_seconds — The whole seconds from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z to self, rounded toward negative infinity.
  • unix_millis — The whole milliseconds from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z to self, rounded toward negative infinity.
  • total_seconds — The length of self in seconds, exactly: PT1.5S is 1.5.
  • total_millis — The length of self in whole milliseconds, rounded toward zero.
  • plus — self moved later by by, earlier where by is negative.
  • minus — self moved earlier by by.
  • since — The duration from earlier to self, negative where earlier is after self.
  • add_days — self moved by n days.
  • add_months — self moved by n months, clamped to the last day of the month it lands in: Date("2026-01-31").add_months(1) is 2026-02-28.
  • add_years — self moved by n years, clamped as add_months is: February 29 moved by a year is February 28.
  • days_since — The days from earlier to self, negative where earlier is after it.
  • negate — self with its sign reversed.
  • times — self multiplied by n.
  • truncate — The start of the unit containing self: the first day of the month for Month, the Monday of its ISO week for Week.
  • dates — Every date from self up to and excluding end, as range gives the Ints; empty where end is not after self.
  • fmt — self written through a strftime pattern, the directives parse_date reads: Date("2026-10-24").fmt("%d %B %Y") is "24 October 2026".
  • now — The evaluation instant: the host's clock, or --now.
  • today — The date now() falls on in zone, or in local_zone().
  • local_zone — The evaluation zone: --zone, else the TZ environment variable, else the host's, else UTC.

docs.title: Zone
docs.text:
In std/time.

type Zone { name : String }

A time zone: an IANA name the time-zone database holds, "Europe/Berlin", "UTC", or a fixed offset "+02:00". A zone turns a wall-clock DateTime into an Instant and back. The database is the host's where it has one, else the one compiled into the binary, and hql --version names which: system, or the bundled release.

fn Zone(name: String) : Zone

The zone name names: an IANA name, "UTC", or an offset "±HH:MM". Any other text is an evaluation error naming it.

docs.title: std/validators
docs.text:
module validators

Validators: the standard validator traits, imported where they are used, import validators, and never by the prelude, so a program's own Email is its own. A field declared with one, email: Email, is of the one type that implements it; NonEmpty, implemented for more than one type, is named in a rule, validate tags with NonEmpty, where the field's type selects the implementation. A broken one is the violation Contract.f of kind rule.

  • Email — An email address: one @ with text before it, and a domain after it holding a . that neither opens nor closes it.
  • NonEmpty — Text that is more than whitespace, or a list with an element.

docs.title: Implementations
docs.text:
impl Email for String

A String is an Email when it holds exactly one @, does not open with it, and the text after it contains a . and neither opens nor closes with one.

impl NonEmpty for String

A String is NonEmpty when it is not empty once trimmed of whitespace.

impl<T> NonEmpty for List<T>

A List is NonEmpty when it has at least one element.

docs.title: std/vault
docs.text:
module vault

The current vault: the source a program runs against. A host with a vault binds it as vault in the program module; a program running without one has no vault binding, and no module sees it.

  • Vault — A vault: its name, its root, its graph of every card and the links among them, and its cards.

docs.title: Vault
docs.text:
In std/vault.

type Vault { name : String // the vault's directory name root : String // where the vault is graph : Graph // every card as a node, and the links among them // Every card, in the order a sorted walk reaches it: the entries of each // directory sorted by name, depth first. The order is the walk's, never // the filesystem's, so `take(5)` answers the same on every machine. cards : Seq<Card> }

A vault: its name, its root, its graph of every card and the links among them, and its cards.
